HOW TO USE flutter-build-release.yml
(Android build, GitHub Release, and Google Play publishing)
=============================================================

This workflow builds the Flutter app (APK + AAB), creates a GitHub Release,
and — on pushes to `main` only — uploads the AAB to Google Play.

It needs 5 repository secrets before the signing/Play Store steps will work.
Add them at:
  GitHub repo -> Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> New repository secret


1) ANDROID SIGNING SECRETS
---------------------------
These come from your existing local file: android/key.properties
and the keystore it points to: android/app/upload-customer-keystore.jks

  a) ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64
     Base64-encode the keystore file and paste the output as the secret value:

         base64 -w0 android/app/upload-customer-keystore.jks

     (On macOS, use: base64 -i android/app/upload-customer-keystore.jks | tr -d '\n')

  b) ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD
     Value of `storePassword` in android/key.properties

  c) ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS
     Value of `keyAlias` in android/key.properties

  d) ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD
     Value of `keyPassword` in android/key.properties

Never commit key.properties or the .jks file — both are already gitignored.


2) GOOGLE PLAY SERVICE ACCOUNT
-------------------------------
  e) PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON

  How to create it:
    1. Go to Google Play Console -> Setup -> API access.
    2. Create (or link) a Google Cloud service account.
    3. In Google Cloud Console, create a JSON key for that service account
       and download it.
    4. Back in Play Console -> API access, grant the service account
       "Release manager" permission (or a custom role that can manage
       production/testing releases) for this app.
    5. Copy the ENTIRE contents of the downloaded JSON file and paste it
       as the secret value (paste the raw JSON, not base64).

  IMPORTANT (first release only):
  The Google Play API cannot create a brand-new app listing or upload the
  very first AAB for an app. If "Ryto Customer" (com.ryto.customer) has
  never been uploaded to Play Console before, you must manually create the
  app and upload one AAB through the Play Console website first. After
  that, this workflow can publish all future updates automatically.


3) RUNNING THE WORKFLOW
------------------------
  - Automatic: push to `main`, `staging`, or `dev`.
      * `main`   -> builds, creates a GitHub Release, AND uploads to Play Store.
      * `staging`/`dev` -> builds and creates a GitHub Release only (no Play upload).
  - Manual: Actions tab -> "Flutter Build & Release (Ryto Customer App)"
    -> "Run workflow". You can choose the Play Store track:
       internal | alpha | beta | production
    (only used when run on the `main` branch; default is "internal").

  Recommended: keep the default track as "internal" until you're confident
  in the pipeline, then promote to production releases from Play Console,
  or re-run manually with track=production.


4) WHERE TO FIND THE BUILD OUTPUT
-----------------------------------
  - APK:  build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk
  - AAB:  build/app/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab
  Both are attached to the GitHub Release automatically.


TROUBLESHOOTING
----------------
  - "Keystore was tampered with, or password was incorrect" ->
    double-check ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 was generated with no line wraps
    (use `base64 -w0`, not plain `base64`).
  - "App not found" / 404 from Play upload step ->
    the app hasn't been created in Play Console yet (see section 2).
  - Play upload step is skipped ->
    it only runs when the branch is `main` and the event is not a pull
    request; check you pushed/dispatched against `main`.
